thesis.problem: Europe can build satellites and cannot reliably launch them. Ariane 6 is sized for large payloads on a national cadence, Soyuz stopped being available in 2022, and the small and medium satellites that make up most of what Europe now wants in orbit, earth observation, connectivity and increasingly sovereign defence capacity, have had to buy rides from American providers on American schedules and American terms.
thesis.solution: Isar Aerospace builds Spectrum, a two-stage rocket sized for the payloads Europe actually flies rather than the ones a national programme was designed around, and manufactures it itself: engines, tanks and avionics in-house, additive manufacturing rather than a supplier chain across a dozen countries, on the argument that vertical integration is what makes launch cheap and the cadence predictable. It is a spinout of the Technical University of Munich and launches from Andøya in northern Norway.

undisclosed.note: No source has published a figure. TechCrunch lists Isar among Europe's 2025 unicorns.

The crossing, and an unusual one: the instrument that carried Isar Aerospace over the threshold was a convertible bond rather than a priced equity round, so there is no post-money to disclose and nobody has disclosed one. TechCrunch states the fact and the month in the same sentence as the instrument, which is what this record rests on. The company's own university says the same thing, since TUM's press release is titled “Isar Aerospace becomes a unicorn”, but a university announcing its spinout is not on the register's allowlist, so it is mentioned here and not cited.

sources.title: Germany's Isar Aerospace raises $91M to get its satellite launch vehicle off the ground
sources.quote: Isar Aerospace, which is building a micro-satellite launcher significantly smaller and thus lower in price than bigger launchers on the market today, has picked up €75 million ($91 million) in funding.

sources.title: Isar Aerospace raises $165 million to bring more sovereign launch to Europe
sources.quote: German launch startup Isar Aerospace has scored $165 million (€155 million) in new funding as it races toward the inaugural flight of its Spectrum small rocket later this year.

sources.title: Isar Aerospace raises €270m to scale launch operations
sources.quote: German rocket startup Isar Aerospace has raised €270m in fresh funding as Europe races to bolster its sovereign space capabilities amid growing geopolitical tensions.

sources.title: More than 10 European startups became unicorns this year
sources.quote: German space startup Isar Aerospace became a unicorn in June after reaching an agreement with Eldridge Industries for a convertible bond of €150 million (approximately $173 million).
